thread:
maria: Heads-up — during a key-rotation rehearsal in prod-like, we saw a spike in AWS KMS Throttling errors causing ~5% of encrypt calls to fail and a cascade of retries. Not a full outage but a near-miss. @ops-runner @evan :eyes:

devsec-bot: ALERT: kms_encryption_errors rate increased from 0.02% -> 4.8% (5m avg) — first seen 2026-11-22 14:07:03 UTC :rotating_light:

evan: Quick summary — our DEK envelope cache per node had TTL=60s. A rollout caused many pods to restart in parallel, leading to large-scale cache cold starts and simultaneous KMS GenerateDataKey calls. Client retry logic used a short fixed backoff (200ms) which amplified the storm.

kevin: Logs snippet from runtime: 
```
ERROR encrypt failed: kms.ThrottlingException: rate exceeded
call_id=abc123 instance=runtime-7
```

rachael: Did we have circuit breakers around KMS? I thought runtime had one to protect us.

maria: We do, but CB thresholds were tuned for transient errors and didn't trip because retries happened quickly. Also, the degraded fallback we exercised allowed serving using a previously cached unwrapped DEK for read-only paths — that meant a short window where requests bypassed encryption guarantees. Need to avoid silent plaintext fallback.

evan: Mitigations we pushed (hotfix): raised per-node envelope cache TTL to 5m and increased cache size, added full-jitter exponential backoff and reduced retry attempts. Patch preview: 
```
retry: {
  base: 200ms,
  factor: 2.0,
  max: 10s,
  attempts: 6,
  jitter: "full"
}
```

kevin: Also enabled a peer-DEK fetch on cold start — node will attempt to fetch the latest DEK from the cluster-shared encrypted store (consensus-backed) before calling KMS. That reduces thundering KMS calls during mass restarts. This requires RBAC review for the peer-store service account.

rachael: Created GH issue: "near-miss: envelope cache eviction -> kms retry storm" with checklist (audit logs, runbook updates, RBAC PR). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4212 :memo:

maria: Action items: 1) audit all KMS GenerateDataKey calls during rotation window and attach to incident ticket (done) 2) update runbook to remove any automatic plaintext fallback and require explicit degraded mode with signoff 3) add a chaos test that simulates simultaneous container restarts and cache eviction 4) RBAC review for peer-DEK sharing (kevin + security)

ops-runner: We also opened a temporary quota increase with AWS support this morning as a safety net. If folks want, I can keep the ticket open until we verify the peer-DEK path and backoff behavior in staging.

kevin: Will follow up on RBAC PR and add guardrails in the peer-fetch code (auth checks + audit events).

rachael: I'll update the runbook and add a postmortem-light near-miss note. Assigning to evan + kevin for patches.

maria: Thanks everyone. Important lessons: avoid synchronized restarts during key ops, use full-jitter exponential backoff, prefer peer/cluster caches before hitting KMS, and never silently degrade to plaintext. Pushing a short retro and runbook PR now. :thumbsup:
